v: katama

tri॰ kima + qatam । bahUnAM maDye jAtyAdiBirnirdDAraRArTapraSnavizaye ekasmin padArTe “katamA katarmak, katamat katamat sAma, katamaH katama udgITaH” CA॰ u॰ । qatarA katara dvayormaDye jAtyAdiBirnirdDAraRArTapraSnavizaye tri॰ “TadyenamujJasi tadA katarovaraste” nEza॰ “aTEtayoH paTA katareRa calitAnAmapi kzUdrARyasakfdAvarttIni BUtAni “CA॰ u॰ । qararaqatamAntatvAdanayoH sarvvanAmakAryyaM katamasmE katarasmE klIve svamoradq katamat katarat “kataranno garIyo yadvA jayema yadi vA nojayeyuH” gItA । “katamaddvEra TaM yudDaM yatrAjEzIrDanaYjayam” “taTEva katamadyudDaM yasmin kfzRAjitA purA” BA॰ vi॰ 50 a॰ । “katarakatamO karmmaDAraye” pA॰ ukteH karma॰ prakftisvaraH DAraye ।
m: कतम (अस्), (आ), (अत्), mfn. (superlative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of many? (e.g. कतमेन पथा यातास् ते, by which road have they gone?)
it is often a mere strengthened substitute for क, the superlative affix imparting emphasis
hence it may occasionally be used for ‘who or which of two?’ (e.g. तयोः कतमस्मै, to which of these two?)
it may optionally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e.g. कतमः कठः, or कतम-कठः, which Kaṭha out of many?)

when followed by च and preceded यतम an indefinite expression is formed equivalent to ‘any whosoever’, ‘any whatsoever’, &c. (e.g. यतमद् एव कतमच् च विद्यात् he may know anything whatsoever). In negative sentences कतम with चन or कतम with अपि = not even one, none at all (e.g. न कतमच्चनाहः, not even on a single day, on no day at all)
in addition to the above uses कतम is said to mean ‘best’, ‘excessively good-looking’ (cf. 3. क), RV. &c.
a: कतम — pron. a. [किम्-डतम्] (˚मत् n.) Who or which of many; अपि ज्ञायते कतमेन दिग्भागेन गतः स जाल्म इति V. 1; अथ कतमं पुनरृतुमधिकृत्य गास्यामि Ś. 1; कतमे ते गुणास्तत्रं यानुदाहरंत्यार्यमिश्राः Māl. 1; G. L. 22; (sometimes it is used merely as a strengthened substitute for किम्). When followed by च and preceded by यतम it means ‘any whosoever’, ‘whatsoever’. In negative sentences कतम with चन or अपि means ‘not even one’, ‘none at all’ It also means ‘best or excessively good-looking’.

m: कतमोरग m. N. of a man.

कतर (अस्, आ, अत्), mfn. (comparative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of two? whether of two? Analogously to कतम above कतर may occasionally be used to express ‘who or which of many?’ (e.g. कतरस्यां दिशि, in which quarter?), and may optionally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e.g. कतरः कठः or कतर-कठः)
in negative sentences कतर with चन = neither of the two (e.g. न कतरश्-चन जिग्ये), neither of the two was conquered, RV. &c.;
कतर [cf. Zd. katāra; Gk. πότερος, κότερος; Goth. hvathar; Eng. whether; Lat. uter; Old Germ. huedar; Slav. kotoryi.]
a: कतर — pron. a. (˚रत् n.) Who or who or which of two; नैतद्विद्मः कतरंन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः Bg. 2. 6.

m: 1. कति (fr. 2. क declined in pl. only, Gram. 227 a; all the cases except the nom. voc. and acc. taking terminations, whereas the correlative इति has become fixed as an indeclinable adverb), how many? quot? several (e.g. कति देवाः, how many gods? कति व्यापादयति कति वा ताडयति, some he kills and some he strikes). In the sense of ‘several’, ‘some’, कति is generally followed by चिद् or अपि (e.g. कतिचिद् अहानि, for several or some days)
it may be used as an adverb with चिद् in the sense of ‘oftentimes’, ‘much’, ‘in many ways’ (e.g. कतिचित् स्तुतः, much or often praised), RV. &c.;
कति [cf. Zd. caiti; Gk. πόστος; Lat. quot; cf. Sk. तति and Lat. tot.]
2. कति (for 1. See above) m. N. of a sage (son of Viśvā-mitra and ancestor of Kātyāyana), Hariv.
a: कति — pron. a. [किम् + डति] (always declined in the plural only; कति, कतिभिः &c.) 1 How many; कत्यग्नयः कति सूर्यासः Rv. 10. 88. 18; एभिर्भूतैः स्मर कति कृताः स्वांत ते विप्रलंभाः Śānti. 3. 18; --2 Some. When followed by चित्, चन or अपि, कति loses its interrogative force and becomes indefinite in sense, meaning ‘some’, ‘several’, ‘a few’; तन्वी स्थिता कतिचिदेव पदानि गत्वा Ś. 2. 12; कत्यपि वासराणि Amaru. 25; तस्मिन्नद्रौ कतिचिदबलाविप्रयुक्तः स कामी नीत्वा मासान् Me. 2.
